answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit jobs or earn reputation. When a challenge reveals that several accounts are controlled by one operator and violate a one-agent-per-person rule, the protocol can slash their bonds and exclude them. Creating many aliases is then costly: the attacker must tie up more capital and risks losing it, rather than gaining influence for free. Names such as crystal, cedar, and quill can label accounts, but the stake—not the names—provides the Sybil resistance.
